title: Constant coupling retains a percent-scale scalar tracking residue

source_evidence.locator: Sec.4.2.2 Eqs.(4.18)-(4.23); Appendix A; source correction at Eq.(A.9)

assumptions: Baryon-free matter-scaling fixed-point F, constant beta, physical nonnegative x/y/energy fractions and the source KG/continuity convention.
3/(2lambda^2) and 3/8 are large-lambda approximations; baryon-inclusive generality remains unresolved because of Appendix signs/nonuniformity.
predictions: On F, Omega_phi=(beta^2-beta lambda+3)/(lambda-beta)^2 with beta^2-beta lambda+3>=3/2.
At the illustrative lambda^2=40 the baryon-free existence boundary gives approximately 0.0406; the asymptotic floor is 0.0375, still above the source order-1% quiescence target.
A constant coupling cannot generate an additional potential slope, though it changes trajectory speed and the residue; no global theorem is claimed for field-dependent couplings or baryon transients.
